issues.legal_issue: An adoption governed by mandatory statutory formalities is not established by evidence of upbringing and treatment as a child when the required consent and actual giving and taking in adoption are not proved.
material_facts: The claimant’s biological parents died when she was very young, and her grandmother gave her to her maternal aunt and the aunt’s husband to be brought up.
The aunt and her husband raised the claimant, and school, college, government, and employment records identified them as her parents.
The claimant admitted that she had no proof of the ceremony of giving and taking in adoption, and the plaint did not plead that the adoption complied with the governing legal requirements.
The aunt and the claimant’s grandmother testified that the claimant had been brought up by the aunt and her husband but had not been adopted.
The claimant sought to rely on her upbringing and records as evidence of adoption.
issues.conclusion: The claimant failed to prove a valid adoption. Evidence that she was raised and treated as a daughter could not replace proof of the mandatory conditions for an adoption governed by the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. The Court distinguished L. Debi Prasad, which concerned an adoption alleged to have occurred before that Act, and relied on Ghisalal for the mandatory nature of the wife’s consent. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 6, 7, 9, and 11(vi) of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 require compliance with the conditions for a valid adoption, including the adopting husband’s wife’s consent and the child being actually given and taken in adoption with intent to transfer the child to the adoptive family. Ghisalal v. Dhapubai (Dead) by Lrs. & Ors. holds that the wife’s consent is mandatory. L. Debi Prasad (Dead) by Lrs. v. Smt. Tribeni Devi & Ors., concerning an adoption alleged to have occurred in 1892, did not permit an inference from subsequent treatment to overcome the statutory requirements applicable to an adoption under the 1956 Act.

rule.if: adoption_validity_claim and mandatory_formality_regime and not actual_giving_and_taking_proved and not adopter_spouse_consent_proved

predicates.adoption_validity_claim: A party asks the court to recognize that a child was adopted.
predicates.mandatory_formality_regime: The alleged adoption is governed by a legal regime that makes specified adoption formalities mandatory.
predicates.actual_giving_and_taking_proved: The party claiming adoption establishes that the child was actually given and taken in adoption with the required intent.
predicates.adopter_spouse_consent_proved: The party claiming adoption establishes the required consent of the adopting person's spouse.

issues.definition: When an adoption claim is governed by mandatory formalities and actual giving and taking and the required spouse’s consent are not proved, the claimed adoption is not established as valid.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who does not establish adoption cannot obtain a declaration of adopted-child status or partition of an estate on the basis of that status.
material_facts: The claimant sought a declaration that she was the adopted daughter of the deceased and his wife, and sought partition of the deceased’s properties as a result.
The deceased died intestate, and the claimant asserted that she was entitled to a share of his estate as his adopted daughter.
The claimant failed to prove a valid adoption.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled to the declaration or partition sought on the basis of the alleged adoption, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The claimed entitlement to recognition as an adopted child and to partition of the alleged adoptive parent’s estate depended on proof of a valid adoption. Because the claimant did not prove adoption in compliance with Sections 6, 7, and 11 of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956, the asserted status could not support the requested relief.

predicates.adoption_based_declaration_partition_cla: A claimant seeks recognition as an adopted child and partition of an alleged adoptive parent's estate on that basis.
predicates.valid_adoption_proved: The claimant establishes that the adoption was valid.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks declaration and partition on the basis of adoption but does not establish a valid adoption, those adoption-based remedies are denied.
